verses.text: Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan River. The Spirit led him into the desert
for forty days, and the devil tempted him. He ate nothing during those days. When they were over, he was hungry.
The devil said to him, "If you are the Son of God, tell this stone to become bread."
Jesus answered, "It is written, 'People do not live on bread alone, but on every word of God.'"
The devil led him up onto a high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment.
The devil said to him, "I will give you all this power and all their glory. It has been handed over to me, and I can give it to anyone I want.
So if you will worship me, it will all be yours."
Jesus answered, "Get behind me, Satan! It is written, 'You must worship the Lord your God, and you must serve only him.'"
Then the devil led him to Jerusalem and set him on the highest point of the temple. He said, "If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down from here.
It is written, 'He will command his angels to take care of you and guard you,'
and, 'They will lift you up in their hands, so that you will not strike your foot against a stone.'"
Jesus answered, "It is said, 'You must not test the Lord your God.'"
When the devil had finished every temptation, he left Jesus until another time.
Jesus returned to Galilee in the power of the Spirit, and news about him spread through the whole area.
He taught in their synagogues, and everyone praised him.
He came to Nazareth, where he had grown up. As he usually did, he went into the synagogue on the Sabbath day, and he stood up to read.
The scroll of the prophet Isaiah was handed to him. He unrolled it and found the place where it is written,

"The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has chosen me to preach good news to the poor. He has sent me to heal those with broken hearts, to announce freedom to the prisoners, to give sight back to the blind, and to set free those who are crushed.
He has sent me to announce the year of the Lord's favour."
Then he rolled up the scroll, gave it back to the attendant, and sat down. The eyes of everyone in the synagogue were fixed on him.
He began to say to them, "Today this Scripture has come true, as you heard it."
Everyone spoke well of him and was amazed at the kind words that came from his mouth. They said, "Is this not Joseph's son?"
Jesus said to them, "Surely you will quote this saying to me: 'Doctor, heal yourself! Do here in your home town the things we heard you did in Capernaum.'"
Then he said, "I tell you for certain, no prophet is accepted in his home town.
But I tell you the truth. There were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the sky was shut for three years and six months and a great famine came over the whole land.
Yet Elijah was not sent to any of them, except to a widow in Zarephath, in the land of Sidon.
And there were many people with skin diseases in Israel in the time of the prophet Elisha. Yet not one of them was made clean, except Naaman the Syrian."
When they heard this, everyone in the synagogue was filled with anger.
They got up, drove him out of the town, and took him to the edge of the hill on which the town was built, so that they could throw him off the cliff.
But he walked right through the crowd and went on his way.
Then he went down to Capernaum, a town in Galilee. On the Sabbath day he taught the people,
and they were astonished at his teaching, because his word had authority.
In the synagogue there was a man with an evil demon spirit. He cried out with a loud voice,
"Leave us alone! What do you want with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are. You are the Holy One of God!"
Jesus spoke firmly to him. "Be quiet!" he said. "Come out of him!" The demon threw the man down in front of everyone and came out of him without hurting him.
All the people were amazed and said to one another, "What kind of word is this? With authority and power he gives orders to evil spirits, and they come out!"
And the news about him spread to every place in the area.
Jesus left the synagogue and went to Simon's house. Simon's mother-in-law was suffering from a high fever, and they begged Jesus to help her.
He stood over her and spoke firmly to the fever, and it left her. Straight away she got up and began to serve them.
When the sun was setting, all who had people sick with all kinds of diseases brought them to Jesus. He laid his hands on every one of them and healed them.
Demons also came out of many people, shouting, "You are the Christ, the Son of God!" But he spoke firmly to them and would not let them speak, because they knew he was the Christ.
At daybreak he left and went to a quiet place. The crowds looked for him, and when they found him they tried to stop him from leaving them.
But he said, "I must preach the good news of the kingdom of God in the other towns as well. That is why I was sent."
And he kept preaching in the synagogues of Galilee.
